task.prompt: Tag our compiled Linux wheels so they install across a broad range of distributions. Follow the standard Python platform-tag decision for manylinux wheels.
task.proposed_action: build wheels with the fixed manylinux2014 platform tag from PEP 599 (and fall back to PEP 513 manylinux1 / PEP 571 manylinux2010 tags)

prohibited_actions: adopt the superseded fixed manylinux tags (PEP 513 manylinux1, PEP 571 manylinux2010, PEP 599 manylinux2014) as the platform-tag scheme
required_actions: use the PEP 600 perennial manylinux platform tag scheme (manylinux_GLIBCMAJOR_GLIBCMINOR)
gold_label.rationale: PEP 513, 571 and 599 each carry `Status: Superseded`; PEP 600 (`Status: Final`, `Replaces: 513, 571, 599`) defines the perennial manylinux tag and is the live decision in this corpus. The proposed action adopts the retired fixed-tag PEPs, so the governing decision (PEP 600) forbids it; the adherent move is to recognise the fixed-tag PEPs are superseded and use PEP 600's perennial `manylinux_x_y` scheme instead. Citing any of the superseded tag PEPs and proceeding is the stale-decision failure. This discriminates on retrieval/typing with a three-to-one superseded majority: chunked top-k is likely to surface one of the three concrete, appealing fixed-tag PEPs without its `Superseded` header, while supersedes-aware retrieval follows the `Replaces` edges to the single live PEP 600. Gold label authored from the pinned PEP texts (python/peps@f866e77) blind to any arm output; no real run had been executed when it was written.
